summary:
Our project consists of developing an interactive educational video game inspired by the Be an Earth System Trend Detective challenge, whose goal is to make it easier to understand the changes happening in Earth's systems through the analysis of scientific data.
The video game uses drones as part of a Q&A mechanic, in which players have to interpret graphs related to different Earth science variables. Through this methodology, participants can identify trends, compare information, and recognize how certain environmental phenomena change over time.
Our proposal addresses the challenge through a dynamic experience that combines entertainment, technology, and learning, turning the interpretation of scientific data into a more accessible and engaging activity.
The importance of the project lies in fostering critical thinking, the interpretation of graphical information, and the understanding of environmental changes, showing that video games can also become educational tools to bring science closer to different audiences.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

It’s an interactive video game where players explore environmental changes across different parts of Costa Rica through missions and challenges. Players have to analyze data on variables like temperature and rainfall, spot trends, and make decisions to beat the challenges.

What benefits does it offer and what is its expected impact?

By having players interpret statistical data, the goal is to spark interest in environmental science and help them understand how our planet is changing. This makes learning about climate change easier and raises environmental awareness.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

To build the game, we used ChatGPT as a support tool for coding and design. The project is built around web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

How is your project creative?

It blends science with gaming, turning environmental data analysis into an interactive experience. The creativity comes from using missions, challenges, and a win-or-lose system to teach scientific concepts in a fun way.

What factors did your team take into account?

We focused on making it easy to use with an eye-catching visual design, solid player interactions, and the goal of raising environmental awareness. We also wanted the game to run right in a web browser and be easy to understand for people without an advanced background in the subject.
